name: SPX, the opening lane's call: the average price over the next 10 minutes, and the end price in tape units beside it
how_to_use: Step 4 of the opening lane. The state is the lane's live answers from step 2, each rewritten by code as one sentence with how sure JEV was, plus context lines: the end-price request's names the flat, small and big bands in index points for this read and the tape unit in points (the middle of the last three 5-minute slice ranges, held at a fixed share of the day's expected move until 09:45, floored after; spx_jev/cuts.py), the stretch labels' ruler; the average-price request's gives the call's flat zone in points.

Two questions ride on the sentences, in two requests sent at the same time. average_10 is the lane's call: where the average price over the next 10 minutes sits against the price now, every minute counting equally, up, flat or down, graded on that average (spx_jev/integral.py) against its flat zone; its direction decides.

next_10, the end-price sum, is asked exactly as before and is kept beside the call: where price is 10 minutes on, in five steps, graded from the summed odds of the up and down steps and the big steps against the bar 10 minutes after the read. The size it names is the call's second line, measured at the end price; it never decides.

Every zone is sized at each read from the day's own tape and the VIX, in index points (spx_jev/flat_zone.py): the call's so that on the prior sessions' opening reads it lands flat at its base rate (spec/cuts.json), the end-price sum's flat band the call's zone widened back to the end price, its big line a refit multiple of that. The numbers are filled into each question's text ({zone_points}, {big_points}) and named in the context, and the grader sets each sum against the same numbers.
Each is a forecast, graded by the bars, not a trade signal. Their grades and tally live under state/spx_jev/lanes/tape/ and never touch the live lane.

next_10.ask: Where is price ten minutes from now, and how far?
next_10.why: The lane's end-price box, kept beside the call: direction and size in a single answer, sized by the tape, its size the call's second line.
next_10.instructions: Read `context.flat_zone` for where the flat, small and big bands fall in index points for this read, and `context.unit` for what one tape unit is in points right now, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where is price at the end of the next 10 minutes? Answer down_big, down_small, flat, up_small, up_big or unsure.

criteria.down_big: price ends more than {big_points} points below where it is now, the big band down; on this index's opening reads that happens about {tape_down_big_pct}% of the time
criteria.down_small: price ends below where it is now by more than {zone_points} points and no more than {big_points} points, the small band down; about {tape_down_small_pct}% of the time
criteria.flat: price ends within {zone_points} points of where it is now, either way; the common case, about {tape_flat_pct}% of the time
criteria.up_small: price ends above where it is now by more than {zone_points} points and no more than {big_points} points, the small band up; about {tape_up_small_pct}% of the time
criteria.up_big: price ends more than {big_points} points above where it is now, the big band up; about {tape_up_big_pct}% of the time
criteria.unsure: the answers pull hard both ways, so neither the common case nor any one step can be backed

average_10.ask: Where does the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sit against the price now?
average_10.why: The opening call as it is graded: the average price over the ten minutes, its direction deciding. The five-way end-price sum beside it keeps the size, as a second line.
average_10.instructions: Read `context.average` for the price at this read, what the average over the window is and how many index points either way count as flat for this read, then `answers`, one sentence per question JEV has already answered about this moment, each ending with how sure it was. Taken together, where will the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sit against the price now? Answer up, down or flat.

criteria.up: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits more than {zone_points} points above the price now
criteria.down: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits more than {zone_points} points below the price now
criteria.flat: the average price over the next {window_minutes} minutes sits within {zone_points} points of the price now, either way
